President Trump is returning from his first ever face-to-face joint meeting
with the presidents of China and Russia.
Instead of briefing the public about it right after the talks in Shenzhen,
Trump has opted to wait.
NPR's Danielle Kurtzleben says no diplomatic breakthroughs were announced,
but the president was notably friendly with his authoritarian counterparts.
Trump referred to Russian President Vladimir Putin as his friend,
and said that he and Chinese leader Xi Jinping have a "outstanding personal relationship."
Both of those leaders are accused of human rights abuses.
In a statement after the meeting,
the three said they agreed to talk in the future about curbing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.
They also talked about the importance of "immunities of state officials"
and agreed that the International Criminal Court "must not abuse their jurisdiction."
The statement did not mention the wars in Iran or Ukraine.
Trump says that he plans a press conference Friday at noon.
Danielle Kurtzleben and PR News.
On Capitol Hill, Senate Republican leader John Thune was asked if he's worried
Trump may have conceded too much about Ukraine during the talks on the sidelines of the Apex
Summit.
As far as I'm concerned, I'm with Ukraine,
and so I think that's going to be where most of my colleagues find themselves.
Meanwhile, Vladimir Putin has vowed retaliation for Ukraine's attacks
on a bridge that connects Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula.
Russia illegally annexed Crimea in 2014, eight years before the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
The major law firm Kirkland and Ellis performed nearly $12 million in free legal work for the
Trump administration to avoid being targeted with an executive order.
NPR's Kerry Johnson reports Democrats in Congress are demanding answers from other law firms.
President Trump slapped several law firms with punitive orders when he returned to the White
House because they hired lawyers or represented clients he did not like.
Several big law firms chose to settle with the Trump administration
to stave off those orders and workplace probes.
Kirkland and Ellis recently told House Democrats it performed nearly $12 million in free legal work
for the administration, though it balked at helping to rename the Kennedy Center or helping
Trump with some other pet projects. Democrats want to know if other big law firms wound up
doing that work and say they'll make the issue a priority for oversight next year.
Kerry Johnson, NPR News.
The artificial intelligence giant anthropic rose sharply after making the biggest public
stock offering ever today, at one point surpassing $2 trillion in value.
That's despite anxiety about an AI bubble and fear that the technology threatens lives
and livelihoods. Anthropic shares shot higher as trading began and held onto much of those gains
to close up 17 percent. Meanwhile, the rest of the market tumbled. The S&P 500 dropped
2 percent for a six straight loss. That's the longest streak since 2024 and it's down
8.2 percent from its record set last month. The Dow dropped more than two percent.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Florida has carried out its record-breaking 20th execution of the year on a man convicted of
killing a pregnant woman and her husband during a home invasion. Florida has carried out more
than half of the nation's 38 executions this year under Republican Governor Ron DeSantis.
They come amid renewed scrutiny of capital punishment following Tennessee's failed
execution of Christa Pike in September. The video game Grand Theft Auto 6 has already
made nearly $2 billion and it's only been out for one day and PR's James Mastromorino reports.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is the first game in the controversial crime video game series in 13 years.
Finally, so excited.
GTA 6 takes place in a fictionalized version of Miami called Vice City.
Real-life buildings and streets appear in the game, while Miami itself has rebranded as Vice
City in a multi-million dollar marketing campaign. That's just a sliver of its
estimated budget of around a billion dollars. The investment is paying off. The game's on track to
earn more than three billion dollars within its first week. And this is only the beginning.
Experts project that Grand Theft Auto 6 will make billions of dollars for years to come.
James Mastromorino, NPR News. San Diego County has hired more than 500
goats to help clean up brush and grass to prevent wildfires. According to Cal Matters,
the pilot program is meant to reduce vegetation around homes, key roads, and in areas that may
be needed as evacuation sites. They're aided by five dogs who help manage the herd.
I'm Rylan Barton. This is NPR News from Washington.
